properties.statement:
READ FROM SOURCE 2026-08-10, not inferred: two HEAL rules fire UNCONDITIONALLY on an edge type while their message names a condition the code never evaluates.

    heal.rs:971  unresolved_setup   iterates every ANTICIPATES edge and emits
                                    "'X' anticipates 'Y' but nothing follows through"
                                    — there is no follow-through test anywhere in the loop.
    heal.rs:906  contradiction      iterates every CONTRADICTS edge (unless alignment=supporting)
                                    and suggests `generate_decision`, while the rule's own doc
                                    comment at heal.rs:47 describes it as "two nodes joined by
                                    CONTRADICTS with NO RESOLVING DECISION". Nothing looks for one.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE SAME IN BOTH CASES AND IT IS NOT NOISE: THE SUGGESTED FIX PROVABLY DOES NOT CLEAR THE FINDING. Write the resolving Decision the contradiction rule asks for and the contradiction still fires. Build the thing an ANTICIPATES edge anticipates and the unresolved_setup still fires. The only ways out are deleting the edge or acknowledging the defect — so a design is PUNISHED FOR RECORDING THE RELATIONSHIP, and the cheapest way to a clean report is to stop recording anticipation and contradiction at all.

OBSERVED LIVE, WHICH IS HOW IT WAS FOUND. Recording `dec:merge-survivor-provenance` ANTICIPATES `dec:a-tied-merge-breaks-by-degree-not-by-alphabet` — an honest edge, since the older decision's own rationale says "consider ranking unset below authored in a future revision" — took detect_defects from 7 to 8 immediately, and no amount of building will take it back to 7.

THIS EXACT CLASS IS ALREADY FIXED ONCE IN THE SAME FUNCTION, sixty lines above. heal.rs:892-905 documents the CONTRADICTS/alignment=supporting bug: the loop read the edge TYPE and never the PROPERTY, so every correctly-modelled corroboration came back as a structural defect, and `dec:commands-are-the-exception` QUALIFYING `dec:skills-served` turned the graph red. Its recorded lesson is verbatim: "A property the detector ignores is a property that lies." The same sentence applies to a CONDITION the detector never computes — and the damage named there applies here too: the only ways out were to acknowledge a defect that is not one, or to stop recording the relationship.

WHAT A FIX WOULD HAVE TO DECIDE, because neither is obvious and this is not a repair proposal. For unresolved_setup: what COUNTS as follow-through — the anticipated node existing at all (trivially true, the edge points at it), reaching `accepted`, gaining a SATISFIES/REALIZES chain, or arriving in an epoch. For contradiction: what counts as RESOLVING — a Decision edged to both endpoints, or one edged to either, and whether a `proposed` Decision resolves anything. Both questions are real design questions and answering them wrongly converts an over-firing rule into an under-firing one, which is worse.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the ANTICIPATES edge was NOT deleted to restore the count to 7. The edge is true, and removing a true relationship to satisfy a detector that fires unconditionally is the gaming this project warns against everywhere else. The defect belongs to the rule, not to the edge.
